title: Old Boots
subtitle: They once belonged to an unfortunate soul, but perhaps they will grant you better luck.

trails.title: Best Wishes
trails.description: Rumors? Entertainment? Seemingly trivial or deeply meaningful outpourings?

content.text:
████,

Being stuck in recovery is boring, but at least it keeps you from getting shot on the battlefield. By the time your knee gets better, this damned war might finally be over! Assuming I make it—which is a strange thing to say—my first stop would be to come see you. Maybe, if we're lucky, we could even go home together.

Let me share the recent news. There's a soldier that everyone claims "came back from the dead"—whether that's true or people invented the story doesn't really matter to the officers—he has been reassigned to the front as a sergeant under Major Braun.

Why would he accept such a posting? Why even go back to the front at all? I know your mind would be swimming with these questions, but nobody can figure out his motives. He turned down a safe position with the press bureau but has refused to ever pick up a rifle again. He's only interested in retrieving the bodies of the fallen from the field. Can you believe that? Personally, I'd rather be a dressed-up press puppet over ducking artillery shells any day of the week, even if it meant encouraging young men to march to their deaths ...

... Mein Gott, ████, as I write this, it finally dawns on me: I've always known why he refused them after all. I just never thought anyone would have the courage to make that choice.

items.text: Old Boots
Trenches
Soldiers lay a corpse on a dry wooden plank, making an effort to place their fallen comrade in something resembling a peaceful pose.
The plank, formed from dismantled ammo crates, has been formed into a makeshift sledge complete with a small set of wheels.
The handler stands resolutely by the body at the edge of the trench, his tattered cloak making him look the part of a grim reaper.
He kneels, prying off the soldier's dog tag, and pockets the bottom half.
Franz Schreyer.

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: This is all we could find. Can you take care of him, Charon?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Naturally. He will be given a proper burial.

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: I thought they said this war would end before the winter came.
A now familiar gloom seeps out from behind Rudolph's thick glasses, like tears.
Franz lies still, indifferent to the scene.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Heh ...
Another soldier shoves his way through their small crowd, puffing with frustration, places another leg on the board, completing the set.
Then without a word, he removes the boot from the corpse's other leg—matching it with another.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Now he'll be ready for the march home.

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: You sure that was Franz's leg?
The kind-hearted Captain Wilhelm looks at his soldier in horror.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Better be. I risked my life up there grabbing it. He promised I could have his boots if he got scraped off.

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: My God. I remember when he said that.
He starts to say something but swallows it back.
The soldiers huddle together in the narrow bend of the trench.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: But ...
Charon's words come out in a slow drip, seemingly unaware of the conversation around him.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Andreas went missing in the last attack. The body will be impossible to move off the frontlines without him.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Eh, your pony? Good bet it's worm food.

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: Shut up, Erich!

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Please, don't worry. There will be somewhere quiet nearby, but it may take a while to find it.

items.speaker: Wilhelm
items.text: Take your time, Charon. The weather's cool these days.
Wilhelm attempts a pat on Charon's shoulder.
Not far away, Major Eberhard Braun, the company commander, sits on an empty water drum. His eyes fixed coldly on the trench wall ahead.
He drops a cigarette butt and stands.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Charon, come here.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Yes, sir.
He responds to his superior.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: You remember Montpaix? The town near our rear?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Certainly. We fought there in the warmth of summer. Our Lieutenant Colonel died in that battle.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You were in charge of a company, until you were injured and sent to recover. There were many graves to be dug, but the days were warm and dry.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: It was a hard fight to drive our enemy from that town, a damn good one. Even if our lines have only moved a short distance past it since.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: But why this talk of Montpaix all of a sudden?

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Army Command has decided to attend a parley held by the Foundation in Montpaix. Colonel Hirschfelder will be present on behalf of our nation.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: We've handed it over to the Foundation. Pfft, they're calling it a "safe zone."

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Many hope that peace will come before the winter.
The major's response is blunt.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: The only end to this war I can accept is victory—total victory over our enemies.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: They say we've broken through on the eastern front; we only need to push our advantage, and they'll collapse. Once we've freed up all that manpower and material, we'll be able to crush our enemies here too.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: We may run ourselves dry of ammo and blood before then, sir. No cries of victory are loud enough to wake the dead.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Winning here is a part of something far bigger than you could understand.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Is it? When you returned to the front after your injury, you came with eyes red as a furnace. You wore an old face, a mask of war.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You haven't worn that mask in many years, since before our first taste of battle and blood.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: A whole class volunteered. Nothing more than schoolboys, we marched obliviously into the killing field. You should rest.
The major's already-thin lips press together into a sharp, blade-like line.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Enough with the poems, soldier. I called you with an order. You must go to Montpaix.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Mr. Mühlenberge sent us a package, and I need someone to fetch it for me.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: I know you'll do your duty for the fatherland, my friend. Take as many bodies with you as you can; we can't leave them rotting in the trenches.

items.speaker: Major Braun
items.text: Dismissed.
The major gets up and moves down the trench.

"Montpaix looks like it had been a nice little town before the war. Now, its old streets and laneways are pocked with craters and crumbling buildings—cruel reminders of the brutal battles that raged through it."

"Silent screams still echo to me from its laneways, 
a reminder that a man who has seen war will only find peace when he is dead and buried."
Foundation Safe Zone
The town has seen the worst of the war, but with the sudden influx of traffic and activity, it seems to breathe new life.
The streets, barely cleared, are swarming with uniforms, some military, and others checkered gray-and-white.
Are you looking for help, sir?
His head creaks in the direction of the voice, finding a young woman, likely a medic.
Her golden badge marks her as the Foundation's employee, but even more striking is the armor layered over her coat.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Hold on, soldier. I'm Nurse Marsha. Please show your face so I can verify your identity.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Good day, sister. What lies beneath this mask will not give you the answer you seek. Here, let this serve for identification.
He rummages out a notebook from his coat, retrieving a folded ID card from within.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Major Eberhard Braun is waiting on a package from Montpaix. He sends his NCO to collect it. He did not say from whom.
She receives it, studying the card.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I see. Your name is Paul ...

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Charon. That is the name the soldiers use, and the one you should use as well. The name you see there doesn't belong to this war any longer.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I've heard your name before.
She returns the document, then scans around as she wrings her hands.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: You'll find plenty of packages here. Go ahead and look for whichever one belongs to your Major Braun, but there'll be more paperwork to sign before you can leave with it.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: If you're willing to wait, things will get moving again once the parley has finished.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Time is a resource the dead have in abundance.
He looks back at her, his body seeming almost rooted to the spot.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Are you certain you're alright, soldier?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: The war has taken its toll, but there is nothing you can do to fix these old wounds.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You said that you are a medic, Sister Marsha. Is that why you ask?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Yes, of course. Ordinarily I would be at the clinic, but I was asked to lend a hand here.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Where are the dead from your clinic laid to rest?
She reflects on his words.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: We don't have any yet, by the grace of God. Though, I don't expect that to remain the case.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: There is a bare slope just outside of town; I noticed it when we first arrived here. It could serve that purpose were someone to die ...

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: That is good to hear.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: That someone might die?
The delayed reply leads to misunderstanding.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Ah, no. The slope.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: A quiet place is needed. Many of us from the frontlines could find rest there.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: You mean your brothers in arms?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: All who need burial are my brothers in arms. Though they may have once fought on different sides.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Should there be any in your clinic that need it, they will find rest there too. In a coffin under a marker to remember their place, as is fitting. If you will allow it.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: So be it. You're offering them more decency than most others would. I'll show you the spot.
Forest Outside the Safe Zone
The outskirts of Montpaix.
Dense woods conceal most obvious traces, yet small sounds are amplified.

items.speaker: Soldier?
items.text: Who's there?
You've run late.

items.speaker: Soldier?
items.text: I barely made it. This whole area is under heavy guard.
The soldier squints, eyes narrowing at the gray-blue uniformed figure ahead.

items.speaker: Soldier?
items.text: Where's Hector? He never mentioned you. Give me the countersign.
He raises his weapon, framing the stranger in his sights.

items.speaker: Soldier?
items.text: You hear me? Who the hell are you?
Yet his target is unfazed.
Two paths lie ahead for you.

items.speaker: Soldier?
items.text: W-What are you talking about?
In one, you lead me to your commander. In the other ...
She lowers her rifle and bows her head in a motion almost like prayer. It stuns the soldier for a moment.
You are led into perdition.
The final gunshot rings through the thick forest, then fades away.
She crouches, retrieving a pouch from the fallen enemy.
In the mess of documents and maps, she finds the note she needs.
Foundation, parley, Hirschfelder ...
After reading it, she looks northeast. Beyond the treeline lie the ruins of Montpaix.
Today.
